title: How I Approach Different LMS Platforms
summary: Four platform-informed learning-system models across extended enterprise, corporate core, academic cohorts, and just-in-time knowledge support, with direct experience clearly identified for Absorb and Docebo.

content.business_need: Show how audience, learning need, business context, platform capability, and connected systems change LMS design decisions.
content.audience: Partners, customers, employees, academic cohorts, and learners needing performance support.
learning_objectives: Distinguish extended-enterprise, corporate-core, cohort, and knowledge-portal operating models.
Connect audience and learning strategy to platform structure, learner experience, and evidence.
Identify platform-specific administrative decisions and validation points without overstating direct experience.
content.role: Portfolio design analysis based on direct Absorb and Docebo administration and migration work, plus platform-informed examples for other systems.
content.design_approach: Use four strategic environments and eight platform-specific, illustrative interfaces to make different administration priorities visible. Tabs change the scenario, decision, outcome, and inspectable screen views.
content.development_process: Mapped source-grounded LMS administration practices to the four audience models; selected illustrative platform mockups and custom pixel assets; separated direct experience from platform-informed design patterns.
outcomes: A clearer comparison of where different learning-system architectures fit.
Visible decision paths linking configuration to learner and business outcomes.
A public-safe demonstration with fictional screens and explicit experience boundaries.

assets.caption: Portfolio-safe example; not a production screenshot.

source_material_notes: Absorb and Docebo reflect directly supported work in the LMS background and migration context documents. Other platforms are platform-informed design models. All mockups contain fictional, illustrative content and do not represent implementation claims or production accounts.
